mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: certified true copy from the Companies Office plus certificate of incorporation is taken to the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade Authentications Unit for a single apostille. Consular path: certified copy and incorporation certificate are authenticated by MFAT and then legalized by the destination state embassy or consulate in Wellington. The two routes are mutually exclusive and never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certified Extract from Register)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: extract issued by the Companies Office is notarized if required, then submitted to the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade Authentications Unit for apostille. Consular route: same extract is MFAT-authenticated and then legalized by the destination state embassy or consulate in Wellington. These routes are parallel and exclusive; do not apply apostille and consular legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney (notarized)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand notary public on instructions of the company board
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: board resolution is signed and notarized by a New Zealand notary, then the notarial certificate is submitted to MFAT for apostille. Consular route: notarized resolution is submitted to MFAT for authentication of the notary signature, then legalized by the destination state consulate. The two paths are mutually exclusive; no combination of apostille and consular steps is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Constitution of the Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company board, certified by appointed New Zealand corporate legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: constitution is certified as a true copy by the company secretary and legal counsel, then certified signature is apostilled by MFAT. Consular route: certified constitution is MFAT-authenticated and then legalized by the destination state diplomatic mission in New Zealand. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (AML/CFT due diligence confirmation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: bank officer signs the reference letter, bank seal/certification is applied, and the signature is notarized before submission to MFAT for apostille. Consular route: notarized bank reference letter is submitted to MFAT for authentication and then to the destination state consulate for legalization. The two paths are equivalent but exclusive; sequential apostille plus consular legalization is prohibited.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to incorporation, all proposed directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories must be screened against the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit list of designated persons under the Terrorism Suppression Act 2002, the Office of Foreign Assets Control specially designated nationals and blocked persons list, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, and any New Zealand domestic sanctions or UN Security Council resolution implementing regulations. Politically exposed persons and their family members or close associates must be identified through commercial AML software and manual review. Any positive PEP match, sanctions hit, or adverse media event must be escalated to the AML compliance officer and trigger enhanced due diligence, source of funds verification, and senior management approval before incorporation proceeds. All screening results must be recorded in the UBO and AML file with time-stamped evidence.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office online register and name reservation system (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English or Te Reo Maori, and may include both; if the desired name is drawn from another language, a statutory declaration or translator certificate providing an English transliteration must be submitted. The Companies Office applies a four-tier naming test: exact match against the register, phonetic or transliteration equivalence, visually or aurally confusing similarity, and conceptual association with prohibited or restricted terms. All four tiers must be cleared before a name is reserved.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name reservation is declined, the applicant or its legal counsel may submit a written reconsideration request to the Registrar of Companies within 20 working days of the refusal, specifying the legal and factual grounds why the name should be accepted and attaching any consent from a relevant Minister or regulator for restricted terms. The Registrar must issue a reasoned decision within 15 working days. If the administrative reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may seek judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand. No duplicate reservation of an identical or confusingly similar name may be made while the appeal is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox may satisfy the Companies Office minimum registered office rule because New Zealand permits the registered office to be any address in New Zealand, but the Inland Revenue Department and registered New Zealand trading banks will reject a virtual office for this AI data-labeling BPO industry. Banks performing customer due diligence under the AML/CFT Act 2009 require a physical operating address, payroll evidence, lease documentation, and local management direction. The presence of a mere virtual address creates a rebuttable presumption of lack of commercial substance and may trigger income tax residence challenges, withholding tax classification issues, GST registration refusal, and account denial.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Likelihood: moderate; quantified risk of an unannounced on-site inspection by the Inland Revenue Department or local municipal council is estimated at 35% within the first 18 months for a data-labeling BPO claiming GST input credits and having limited physical presence. Checklist: verifiable lease or sublease, signage visible at the registered office, on-site personnel and payroll records, physical information technology equipment or secure cloud-processing infrastructure located in New Zealand, documented local management oversight, and evidence of commercial activity such as client contracts and invoices. Failure to satisfy these items materially increases the chance of an inspection, de-registration, or penalty assessment.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), sections 17, 18, 20, 21, 41, 42, 88, 125, 126, 127, 152, 153, 154, 162, 189, 198, 199 and 200; Financial Reporting Act 2013; Health and Safety at Work Act 2015; Registered Office and Company Name rules under the Companies (Registration) Regulations 1994.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, a division of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the Companies Register and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: NZ Company Incorporation Application (Form NZCN/Online Application for Registration of a Company) filed electronically through the Companies Office portal, together with any adopted constitution, director consents, and shareholder information.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand law imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a limited liability company. Shares may be issued for cash or non-cash consideration as determined by the directors under sections 41 and 42 of the Companies Act 1993. No blocked escrow capital account or capital attestation certificate is required. The company must maintain a proper share register and, if no constitution is filed, the default rules of the Companies Act 1993 apply.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [●] LIMITED (THE COMPANY)

THIS FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION is made on [●] day of [●], [●], by the directors and initial shareholders of [●] Limited, a company incorporated under the Companies Act 1993, New Zealand, having Company Number [●] and New Zealand Business Number [●]. The board has received the certificate of incorporation, the constitution or default company rules, and the initial registers. The following resolutions were proposed, seconded, and unanimously passed by the directors present at a properly constituted meeting pursuant to section 127 of the Companies Act 1993.

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. RESOLVED that the authorised, issued, and paid-up capital of the Company be fixed at [●] ordinary New Zealand dollar shares of no par value, and that the subscription, allotment, and issue of such shares, whether for cash or such non-cash consideration as the directors shall approve, be and is hereby authorised. RESOLVED that all subscription funds be deposited to the Company bank account, that the share register be updated within sixty days of allotment under section 88 of the Companies Act 1993, and that the directors may accept in-kind consideration, including services and intellectual property, after recording the valuation and board approval minutes.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED that the Company open and maintain one or more bank accounts with a New Zealand registered bank, and that [●], [●], and [●], each acting jointly with any one other signatory, or any two designated officers together, be and are hereby authorized to sign cheques, payment instructions, electronic banking mandates, loan agreements, hedging documents, corporate cards, and all related securities and deposit facility agreements. RESOLVED that the bank be provided with a certified copy of this resolution and the certificate of incorporation.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE AND SERVICE ADDRESS. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at [●] street address, New Zealand, and that all statutory notices and legal process be received and served at that address. RESOLVED that the nameplate of the Company be affixed at the registered office and that any future change of registered office be notified to the Registrar of Companies under section 199 of the Companies Act 1993.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. RESOLVED that [●] be appointed as Managing Director, [●] as Finance Director, and [●] as Company Secretary, each to serve until removed or resigned in accordance with the constitution. RESOLVED that the officers are jointly and severally authorised to sign and file the annual return, tax registrations, employment contracts, banking mandates, and any other instrument required for the conduct of the business, and to ensure that minutes, statutory registers, financial records, and share registers are maintained in compliance with Part 21 of the Companies Act 1993.

5. GENERAL AUTHORITY. RESOLVED that the directors and officers take all necessary steps to register the Company for goods and services tax, employer obligations, accident compensation, and any data-labeling outsourcing contracts, and to procure insurance, office leases, and operational policies as required by law.

This resolution shall remain effective until revoked by a subsequent resolution of the board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name and NZBN Pre-Clearance and Entity Eligibility Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register online portal, administered by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) at https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before incorporation, the applicant or licensed corporate formation agent must search the Companies Register to confirm that the proposed company name is not identical or too similar to any existing registered name. The agent must also check that the name does not imply a prohibited activity and, for a standard limited company, the name must end with Limited or Ltd. In addition, the applicant must confirm that at least one director is resident or, if a foreign director, that the director is not disqualified under section 151 of the Companies Act 1993. The NZBN, a unique thirteen-digit identifier, will be allocated during the subsequent incorporation application; however, this pre-clearance step minimises rejection. The agent should prepare alternative names to enable immediate substitution. Physical notarisation is not generally required in New Zealand, but scanned identification must be legible and meet RealMe or Companies Office authentication standards.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and alternative names
Identification documents of each director and shareholder
Residential and service addresses of directors
Consent to act as director forms
Share capital and share allocation statement
Certificate of foreign good standing, if the director is a foreign entity
RealMe verified user login and authorised agent mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application for name reservation is queried, suspended, or rejected, the formation agent may file a revised name using the Companies Office online resubmission function, provide a judicial affidavit or deed poll evidencing consent of any existing rights holder, or submit a written response to the Registrar explaining why the requested name is not confusingly similar. If the name is prohibited by regulation, the agent selects a previously prepared alternative name and re-files without additional delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Incorporation Application and Company Registry Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, online Companies Register portal under MBIE.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The authorised formation agent or director must complete the online NZ Company Incorporation Application, entering the proposed company name, registered office address, directors, shareholders, secretary, share structure, and constitution election. The system validates the personal data against RealMe and the NZBN registry. The agent must submit the statutory registration fee at the time of filing. If a constitution is adopted, the text must be uploaded and the shareholders must approve it; if not adopted, the default rules of the Companies Act 1993 form the governing document. The Companies Office will issue the certificate of incorporation and automatically issue the NZBN upon successful registration. The company comes into legal existence on the date stated in the certificate. The company must then maintain a register of directors, shareholders, and charges.
required_dossiers: Completed Companies Office incorporation application form
Constitution of the company, if adopted
Director consent forms signed by each director
Shareholder consent and share subscription records
Identification and proof of address of all directors and shareholders
Authority from the formation agent, if acting on behalf of the entity
Registration fee payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office returns a query regarding incomplete director information, mismatched identification, or address deficiencies, the applicant must resubmit corrected data within fifteen business days using the portal's amendment function. If the Registrar refuses to issue the certificate, the agent may apply for registration through a fresh application or appeal the decision to the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment within twenty business days, accompanied by legal submissions and corrected documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Employer Registrations with Inland Revenue and ACC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Inland Revenue Department (IR) and Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, the company must apply to Inland Revenue for a New Zealand IRD number. The company must assess whether to register for Goods and Services Tax (GST) if projected annual turnover exceeds NZD 60,000, and must register for employer obligations if it will have employees, including PAYE, KiwiSaver, and employer superannuation. The company must also register as an employer with the Accident Compensation Corporation if it will employ workers, and must classify the work activity under the appropriate ACC levy classification. Inland Revenue requires the NZBN, registered office, and bank account to be disclosed. For a data-labeling BPO, the company must also confirm that its business activity is correctly described under ISIC 8220 for statistical filings to Stats NZ. This step ensures the company can lawfully hire staff, issue payroll, and collect GST on export or local services.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and NZBN
Company bank account confirmation
Directors' IRD numbers and identification
Shareholder details and ownership percentages
Projected revenue and GST registration election
Employment and payroll information, if applicable
Physical or postal address for tax correspondence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD number application is delayed or queried due to unmet identification or bank verification, the company must resubmit the tax registration form through the myIR portal with certified copies of passport or certificate of incorporation. If the GST registration is backdated or amended, the company must lodge a REQ-error correction or late registration application to Inland Revenue and, in cases of ACC levy misclassification, file an ACC classification review and submit payroll documentation to adjust the levy assessment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, company directors, shareholders, and the company secretary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The board must hold its first meeting and record minutes adopting the incorporation, allotting shares, appointing statutory officers, adopting the registered office, and authorising banking arrangements. The company must issue share certificates, open and maintain a share register, register charges if any, and file annual returns with the Companies Office within one month of the anniversary of incorporation. The directors are responsible for maintaining an accurate minute book and for ensuring that any change in directors, registered office, constitution, or shareholding is filed with the Companies Office within the statutory periods. For a solely online BPO company, there is no requirement to publish a physical address, but the registered office must be a physical address in New Zealand where documents may be served. The company should also adopt data governance and AML/CFT policies if it handles client data in a way that triggers reporting entity status under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; however, the target configuration has been assessed as low risk with no mandatory statutory license.
required_dossiers: First board meeting agenda and signed minutes
Share certificates and share register
Director and secretary registers
Notice of registered office and company records location
Bank account opening resolution and signatory list
Annual return reminder calendar
Company constitution or adopted default rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office issues a compliance notice for a late annual return or missing director consent, the company must file the annual return online immediately and pay the prescribed late fee. If there is a dispute over shareholder allotment, the directors may convene an extraordinary general meeting and pass a corrective resolution. Failure to maintain statutory registers can be cured by reconstructing the register from signed consents, bank records, and tax filings, and by submitting a formal declination or restoration application to the Companies Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupational, Building and Workplace Compliance for Office-Based BPO
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: WorkSafe New Zealand, Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ), territorial authority, and the local council building consent department.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For a data-labeling BPO operation, no industrial manufacturing license, chemical permit, or environmental operating consent is required because the activity is an office-based, low-risk service under ISIC 8220. However, the company must ensure its leased or owned office premises hold a current building warrant of fitness if the building has cable cars, lifts, automatic sprinklers, or backup power systems required under a building consent. The company must prepare a workplace health and safety statement under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, carry out a risk assessment for prolonged display screen work, provide ergonomic workstations, and establish an emergency evacuation plan. If the business employs ten or more persons in the premises, the workplace must have a Fire and Emergency New Zealand approved evacuation scheme under sections 65 to 68 of the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017. The company must also have first aid kits, incident registers, and welfare facilities in accordance with WorkSafe New Zealand guidelines. Electrical installations must be certified where required and any hazardous substances, such as cleaning solvents or IT battery storage, must be kept below statutory threshold quantities and disclosed where required by the Hazardous Substances (Hazardous Substances Assessments) regulations.
required_dossiers: Copy of certificate of incorporation and NZBN
Head lease or ownership evidence of registered office
Building warrant of fitness and building compliance schedule
Workplace risk assessment and hazard register
Health and Safety policy and worker engagement procedures
Fire evacuation scheme approved by FENZ, if applicable
Electrical safety certificates and records
First aid and emergency response arrangements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If WorkSafe New Zealand or the territorial authority issues an improvement notice or prohibition notice, the company must immediately remedy the identified workplace risk, provide written confirmation of corrective actions, and request a reinspection. If the building warrant of fitness is lapsed, the company must engage a building manager to obtain a fresh warrant and may be required to obtain a certificate of compliance from the territorial authority. For FENZ evacuation deficiencies, the company must resubmit the evacuation scheme with revised floor plans and staff roll-call procedures within the time stated in the notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - WorkSafe New Zealand for occupational safety, territorial authority for building compliance, and the Ministry for the Environment and Environmental Protection Authority New Zealand for advisory environmental compliance only; no industrial licensing board approval is required for ISIC 8220 data-labeling BPO.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - New Zealand does not require an operating or manufacturing license for a pure digital data-labeling and AI-training BPO office. The company must merely hold valid business registration, tax registrations, and employment registrations; non-resident ownership is permissible under the Companies Act 1993 and does not inherently trigger a sectoral license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Environment Zealand and Environmental Protection Authority (New Zealand)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - Exempt; ISIC 8220 is a low-impact office service activity with no manufacturing, bulk chemical storage, or discharge, therefore no Environmental Impact Assessment or resource consent is required under the Resource Management Act 1991.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no industrial wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste generation. Office waste must be disposed through local council waste services in accordance with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008, and e-waste from computers and labeling equipment must be handled through approved recycling or e-waste collection programs.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for civil defense fire licensing as a manufacturing operation. However, occupational clearance is mandatory: every workplace must comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, include a worker participation system, first aid and emergency procedures. If ten or more workers are present, the office must have an approved evacuation scheme under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017. The building must hold a current building warrant of fitness where prescribed building systems exist, and electrical installations must meet the Electricity Act 1992 safety standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Tauhake Inland Revenue) - myIR online portal at https://www.ird.govt.nz/myir/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a New Zealand-incorporated limited company, the Companies Office issues an NZ Business Number (NZBN) at incorporation and Inland Revenue automatically allocates an IRD number when the company registers a New Zealand registered office. For a foreign non-resident entity not incorporated in New Zealand but carrying on a taxable activity or deriving New Zealand-sourced income, the entity must first register as an overseas company with the New Zealand Companies Office under the Companies Act 1993 (unless an exemption applies), obtain an NZBN, and then submit the Inland Revenue non-resident company registration application through myIR. The application requires proof of incorporation, registered office and principal place of business details, directors' personal details, New Zealand agent for service, tax residence certificate and BEPS-related self-certification, and bank account details. The IRD number is the single TIN used for income tax, GST, PAYE, and other tax types; a separate GST number is not issued. GST registration is added to the same IRD number via myIR when the entity has a GST taxable activity and exceeds the NZD 60,000 annual registration threshold, or elects voluntary registration. For an offshore non-resident supplier of remote services to New Zealand-resident consumers, the same IRD number is used to register under the GST remote-services supplier regime once the NZD 60,000 threshold is satisfied.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None comparable to a US check-the-box election; New Zealand has no check-the-box regime. Hybrid mismatch and branch mismatch rules under the Income Tax Act 2007 subpart FH apply to arrangements and are not elective. A qualifying closely held New Zealand company may elect look-through company (LTC) status under the Income Tax Act 2007 subpart HA, causing income, losses, and imputation attributes to flow through to shareholders; however, the default classification for an ordinary NZ Ltd is entity-level taxation at the 28% corporate income tax rate.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; voluntary registration is available to any person carrying on a taxable activity. Offshore suppliers of remote services to New Zealand-resident consumers must register when taxable supplies to New Zealand consumers exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period (GST Act 1985 ss 51 and 54B).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not operate a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance system, does not mandate API-based preapproval of invoices, and does not require anti-fraud digital stamping. Tax invoices must contain the particulars required by sections 24 and 24B of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, including seller name, address and GST number, buyer name and address for supplies over NZD 1,000, invoice date, description of goods or services, quantity, price, GST-exclusive and GST-inclusive amounts, or a statement that the supply is zero-rated. GST returns are filed electronically through myIR; Peppol e-invoicing is available and voluntary in New Zealand, but it is not a tax clearance or pre-authorisation platform.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated under section 11 of the GST Act 1985 when they are physically exported by the supplier within 28 days of the time of supply and the supplier holds appropriate customs export evidence. Services, including AI data-labeling and RLHF BPO services, are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, provided the services are not supplied in connection with land in New Zealand, moveable goods in New Zealand, or to a person in New Zealand. For digital and remote services, zero-rating is available where the supplier is satisfied the recipient is a non-resident business or non-resident consumer located outside New Zealand and the place of supply is outside New Zealand. Substantiation should include a written master services agreement with the offshore client, a tax invoice marked as zero-rated, evidence of the recipient's non-resident status, and service delivery logs demonstrating that the AI training/data-labeling services are performed for and used by the offshore customer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Entry) lodged through the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window - required only for physical exports; not applicable to pure service exports
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for any tangible goods consigned offshore
Master services agreement and purchase order evidencing the non-resident recipient and scope of AI data-labeling services
Foreign-currency receipt evidence: SWIFT MT103, bank credit advice, or Wise payout transaction record; New Zealand does not issue Inward Remittance Certificates (FIRC)
Service delivery and use evidence: IP logs, task completion records, monthly service reports, and records demonstrating that the services were supplied to and consumed by the overseas client
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If Inland Revenue determines that a zero-rated export supply has not been substantiated, the supply is reassessed at the standard 15% GST rate on the full consideration and use-of-money interest applies from the due date of the original return. Shortfall penalties apply under the Tax Administration Act 1994: 20% for failing to take reasonable care or taking an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and up to 150% for evasion. Criminal prosecution may also be pursued for tax evasion under section 143A of the Tax Administration Act 1994, carrying fines and imprisonment. The standard four-year reassessment time bar is removed where fraud or evasion is established, allowing retrospective clawback beyond the usual period. Records must be retained for at least seven years under section 22 of the Tax Administration Act 1994.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a freely convertible current and capital account with no exchange control approval requirement for cross-border settlement. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand and the Financial Markets Authority do not impose foreign currency surrender, prior licensing, or repatriation approval on ordinary trading companies. A New Zealand limited company may receive FDI equity injection, open multi-currency bank accounts, convert NZD/USD/EUR in any amount, and remit dividends, royalties, service fees or principal repayments offshore without a currency commission or a Central Bank permit. The profits remittance channel is blocked only by standard prudential, sanctions, and AML/CFT filters plus IRD non-resident withholding tax and dividend imputation obligations. The practical hurdles are bank-level CDD/EDD for high-volume BPO payouts, the maintenance of beneficial ownership registers, and compliance with Overseas Investment Act screening if the activity ever involves sensitive land or significant business assets, which is unlikely for a pure data labelling BPO. Balance of payments reporting to Statistics New Zealand/RBNZ remains statistical rather than permissive. Thus convertibility is unrestricted while electronic wire handling is fully delegated to supervised banks and money service businesses.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. New Zealand has had no mandatory export proceeds surrender requirement since exchange controls were dismantled in the mid-1980s. Exporters may negotiate settlement terms freely, keep receipts in foreign currency with any registered bank, or convert to NZD at their discretion. No statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies. For balance-of-payments and tax alignment, export invoices should be issued on the entity's New Zealand IRD tax file and overseas receipts reconciled monthly; cryptocurrency or quasi-cash settlement is not accepted as valid proceeds under bank policy.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a supplementary payout sub-rail; Low as a primary treasury clearing wall. Wise, registered as a New Zealand financial service provider, and PayPal as a payment facilitator may execute mass payouts to AI annotators; however, neither holds a New Zealand banking licence under the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989, cannot accept deposits as a corporate operating account in the same way as a licensed bank, and must not be used to warehouse client funds. An offshore EMI that markets a NZ entity without FSP registration is barred from servicing the entity; the entity should verify the EMI's NZ AML/CFT registration, overseas licence, sanctions programme and local clearing presence. For NZD payroll to domestic contractors and cross-border mass disbursements under USD 50,000, Wise Business or mass PayPal payout may be used; core capital injection, dividend flow and executive salary payments should remain on SWIFT-channelled tier-1 bank rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory physical presence mandate is prescribed by the Reserve Bank or the FMA for a standard NZ limited company account opening. Remote opening is permissible under the AML/CFT (Sources of Funding and Identity Verification) Code of Practice 2013 if the bank uses electronic KYC or a certified copy of a passport plus independent identity verification. However, banks frequently impose an officer interview by video call and may require an in-person visit where beneficial owners sit in a high-risk jurisdiction. Consular proxy opening may be accepted where a New Zealand lawyer, notary or chartered accountant certifies the identity documents and the apostilled power of attorney/board resolution is supported by a live video verification; pure mail-in proxy without verification is generally insufficient. The statutory directors are therefore not legally compelled to appear physically in-branch, but an explicit bank-level interview may be a practical condition where adverse media or complex ownership is identified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership concentration mismatch between the non-resident parent and the low-asset NZ BPO operating company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholding register and corporate registry search from the NZ Companies Office; passport and proof of residential address for each direct and ultimate beneficial owner; source-of-wealth statement for shareholder funds; 12 months bank/financial statements of the parent; sworn declaration of no bearer shares; sanctions screening report for all owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume fragmented outbound payouts to independent AI annotators/contractors with no conventional employee records and possible feedback loop of remitted funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent contractor master agreements and engagement letters; service invoices and RLHF/CV annotation task logs; batch payroll run files with unique worker identifiers; worker bank/wallet details screened against sanctions; beneficial ownership declarations for high-value contractors; Privacy Act 2020 compliant data-processing contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through risk or unofficial money service business pattern where inbound capital is rapidly distributed to multiple third-party beneficiaries, suggesting disguised payment intermediation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Entity constitution and NZ registration confirming the enterprise is not a money remitter; independent CA opinion that no third-party funds are held and the entity does not fall below FMA money remittance licensing thresholds; board resolution on client fund segregation; commitment to batch direct-credit rails; an AML/CFT process map showing inbound funds are first recorded as equity, then disbursed only against executed service orders and payables aging.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: USD/global clearing and sanctions interception risk, especially if the BPO subcontractor chain touches sanctioned jurisdictions or dual-use AI datasets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current sanctions screening logs for all counterparty banks, beneficial owners, and contractor payees against UN/EU/OFAC/NZ consolidated lists; geolocation and IP provenance controls on the data-labelling workforce; FATCA and CRS forms; transaction-monitoring exception reports; external audit trail for a six-month period; legal opinion confirming no defence/trade sanctions exposure in the training data supply chain.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident parent should remit equity capital via SWIFT MT103 to the NZ tier-1 bank's dedicated Capital Escrow Account, with beneficiary legal name matching the NZ Companies Office record, the company IRD number in field 70, and the ISO 20022 payment purpose code 'EQUI' or the bank's direct-investment BOP code for equity capital. Because New Zealand has no capital controls, no RBNZ approval or foreign exchange permit is required; the only mandatory clearance is bank AML/CFT CDD/EDD, sanctions screening, and beneficial ownership identification. The entity should then execute a share allotment resolution, issue share certificates, and obtain a capital verification report from a NZ chartered accountant or registered auditor. If the investment touches sensitive land or significant business assets, an Overseas Investment Act 2005 consent is required before settlement; a pure data-labelling BPO should not trigger it. No escrow account is statutorily mandated but it provides clean auditability.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational BPO settlements should ride SWIFT MT103 through the NZ bank's global payments network for executive salaries, platform vendor fees, dividend repatriation and contractor outsourcing; for low-value worker payouts, a local-currency clearing rail via Wise Business or PayPal Mass Pay is acceptable up to prudent thresholds and never through personal accounts. For physical trade/equipment procurement, a commercial letter of credit (SWIFT MT700) and documentary collections under URC522 are permissible, but they are not expected for pure data-labelling services. Every outbound payment must carry a consistent purpose narrative classified as business services (ISIC 8220), the pre-validated beneficiary bank details, an end-to-end reference matching the invoice/order number, and a payee name in exact registered form. Cash, crypto, shell-bank transfers and routed payments through private ATMs are prohibited.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla FX forwards up to 12 months for genuine NZD/USD/EUR payroll and subscription exposures, executed under the bank's FMA dealer licence and covered by a board-approved treasury policy; no speculative leverage beyond a 2:1 cover ratio.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permitted only for bona fide hedging of an underlying invoiced exposure in a restricted-currency country where physical delivery is structurally impossible; settlement must be a NZD/USD net differential and supported by an underlying contract/invoice before booking; speculative NDF books are barred.

Cross-currency swaps are permissible for matched-term balance-sheet hedging of shareholder loans, dividends and long-term commercial contracts; the underlying loan agreement, IRD withholding tax certificate and FMA derivative disclosure must be provided; swap duration cannot materially exceed the underlying exposure or loan maturity, and ISDA credit support annexes apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under Companies Act 1993, ss 208-213
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 working days after the anniversary of incorporation, being the company's annual return date; filing is completed electronically on the New Zealand Companies Register.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deliver the annual return is an offence. The company and each director may be fined up to NZD 10,000 approximately USD 6,000 on conviction. The Registrar may also issue a 20-working-day notice and, if no response is made, administratively remove the company from the New Zealand register under s 318 Companies Act 1993. Administrative removal vests company assets in the Crown and requires restoration proceedings to regain active status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company income tax return IR4 and payment of terminal and provisional tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return must be filed by 7 July following the balance date, or 31 March of the following year under an approved tax agent extension; terminal tax is payable by 7 February following the balance date, and provisional tax instalments fall due on 28 August, 15 January and 7 May in the prescribed sequence.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an initial late filing penalty of NZD 250 approximately USD 150 followed by escalating late filing penalties for continuing default. Unpaid tax attracts an initial late payment penalty of 5%, an additional 1% monthly penalty, and use-of-money interest under the Tax Administration Act 1994. Persistent non-filing may lead to default assessments, civil penalties and prosecution, though tax default alone does not directly trigger Companies Office strike-off; prolonged non-filing of annual returns after enforced tax action can lead to removal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Goods and Services Tax returns, if the company is GST registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: GST returns are due on the 28th day of the month after the end of each taxable period; the company may be registered on a one-monthly, two-monthly or six-monthly filing cycle depending on projected turnover and the elected filing frequency.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 250 approximately USD 150 for each overdue GST return, plus a 5% initial late payment penalty, 1% monthly penalty, and use-of-money interest. The Inland Revenue Department may issue default assessments and use escalation and recovery measures such as automatic deduction or debt collection action if arrears persist.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Event-driven statutory notifications covering share allotments, director changes, and registered office changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Return of allotment must be filed within 10 working days of each share allotment; notice of any director change must be filed within 20 working days; and notice of any registered office change must be filed within 20 working days. These obligations are integrated into the recurring annual corporate secretarial maintenance calendar.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-delivery may expose the company and its directors to a fine of up to NZD 10,000 approximately USD 6,000, with continuing penalty exposure for repeated failure and the Registrar's power to correct or decline inaccurate office records. Persistent non-compliance with registrable events may be used as supporting grounds for administrative removal from the register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is mandatory for an FMC reporting entity such as a listed issuer, managed investment scheme, bank, or licensed insurer under the Financial Reporting Act 2013. A company is also large where, in each of the two immediately preceding accounting periods, it satisfies at least two of these quantitative criteria: total assets exceed NZD 60 million approximately USD 36 million; total revenue exceeds NZD 30 million approximately USD 18 million; and 50 or more full-time equivalent employees. Such large companies must prepare audited general purpose financial statements. In addition, shareholders holding at least 5% of the voting shares may validly request a special audit under s 200 Companies Act 1993. Otherwise, a small or medium New Zealand company is not legally required to undergo a certified CPA audit and is not required to file financial statements with the Companies Office.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: FMC reporting entities and large companies must prepare general purpose financial statements in accordance with NZ IFRS, being New Zealand equivalents of International Financial Reporting Standards, or NZ IFRS with the Reduced Disclosure Regime for qualifying non-FMC large entities. Non-large, non-FMC entities that voluntarily prepare financial statements may use the differential reporting simplifications permitted by the XRB Accounting Standards Framework, including NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime; for tax purposes the Inland Revenue Department requires sufficient records to determine taxable income but does not prescribe a complete general purpose financial reporting framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not impose a separate public annual UBO declaration to the Companies Register for a standard private limited company. However, under the Companies Act 1993 the company must maintain an accurate register of members and update it within a 30-day reporting window for any share transfer or allotment, and returns of allotment must be filed with the Registrar within 10 working days. Director changes must be notified within 20 working days. Under the AML/CFT Act 2009, the company as an AI data labelling BPO service provider must identify and verify beneficial owners holding 25% or more ownership or control interest at establishment and must perform periodic customer due diligence refresh on a risk basis, at least annually for higher-risk relationships and whenever a triggering event occurs. The board should formally confirm the internal beneficial ownership record against the shareholder register and Companies Office record at least once each financial year and document any divergence in the minute book.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and their particulars
Register of Charges, Mortgages and other encumbrances
Minute book of shareholder and board resolutions
Register of share transfers and allotments
Beneficial ownership register, where the company is an AML/CFT reporting entity

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 1,200 for a standard New Zealand registered office and corporate secretarial agent retainer; transaction-intensive BPO entities with global employment structures may require USD 1,500 - USD 4,000 per annum.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 for a non-listed small-to-medium New Zealand company requiring a voluntary or shareholder-requested audit; USD 30,000 - USD 90,000 or more for a large or FMC reporting entity with a complex BPO group.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% (Income Tax Act 2007, company income tax rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand has no patent box, free-zone, or preferential 0% corporate regime. Material incentives are the R&D Tax Incentive (15% credit on eligible R&D expenditure, subject to IRD approval and annual claim limits) and full imputation credits at 28%. Tax losses can be carried forward indefinitely under sections IA 3-IA 6 of the Income Tax Act 2007 if the company satisfies the 49% shareholder continuity rule or the business continuity test; the schema placeholder of 5 is not a New Zealand statutory cap.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 - New Zealand Company Income Tax Return, filed through the Inland Revenue Department myIR portal or an approved e-filing software provider
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return due date is 7 July immediately following the tax year. For a non-standard balance date, the return is due no later than six months after balance date unless a tax agent extension is granted by the IRD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total business income from all sources before expenses: sales, service fees, AI data-labeling contracts, RLHF annotation fees, computer-vision bounding-box work, royalties, and interest income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The NZ company must return all gross worldwide income if it is tax resident in New Zealand. If income is attributable to an overseas permanent establishment under a DTA, exclude it only with a documented PE working paper. Never recognise offshore parent revenue as NZ income unless the contracts, resources, and management are genuinely in New Zealand.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenses: employee wages, subcontract data-labour, cloud/AI infrastructure, software, rent, depreciation, marketing, legal fees, and office overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany payments to related parties must be supported by transfer pricing analysis and arm's length rates. Payments of interest or royalties to non-residents require NRWT withholding at the correct treaty-claim rate. Deductions are denied for fines, penalties, non-deductible entertainment, and excessive related-party charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss before tax adjustments: Box 1 minus Box 2.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned BPO/annotation entity should show a normal commercial return consistent with its functional and risk profile. Persistent net losses while the foreign parent earns high returns on NZ-developed data assets will trigger transfer pricing scrutiny.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation adjustments: add back non-deductible amounts, subtract exempt income, foreign-source income exclusions, R&D credits, and imputation credits received.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-deductible additions include income tax, late-payment penalties, NRWT-borne costs, and excessive entertainment. Foreign tax credits require proper substantiation under the foreign tax credit rules. Cross-border leakage adjustments are mandatory.

Compute the positive adjusted taxable income on which the 28% company rate will be applied. If losses are offset, attach the continuity schedule showing the same ultimate non-resident owners held at least 49% of the shares from loss year through offset year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carry-forward or loss offset used.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use prior-year losses only if shareholder continuity is satisfied. A change in the beneficial foreign owner exceeding 51% will cancel all historical losses, unless the business continuity exemption applies. Maintain all ownership continuity records for at least seven years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax calculation: taxable income multiplied by 28%, less tax credits such as RWT, imputation credits, foreign tax credits, PAYE, and provisional tax payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits are non-refundable to non-residents unless a treaty or specific statutory provision allows a refund. NRWT withheld on outbound dividends is a final tax for the non-resident recipient and should be reconciled with the imputation credit account.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation Credit Account (ICA) summary and dividend declaration schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all dividends paid to non-resident shareholders, compute 30% statutory NRWT, show any treaty-reduced rate applied under an approved IR67 declaration, and attach tax residency certificates delivered by the shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors declaration and signature / electronic authentication.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The director declares that the return is true and correct. Knowingly filing false information with intent to evade tax exposes the director to criminal sanctions and personal liability. Review the return for full disclosure of offshore related-party transactions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of an IR4 incurs an immediate late filing penalty of NZ$250, plus further daily/monthly late filing penalties and use-of-money interest if the return remains outstanding. Late payment triggers an initial 5% late payment penalty followed by a recurring 1% per month penalty. Incorrect returns shortfall penalties range from 20% for failure to take reasonable care, 40% for unacceptable tax positions, 100% for abusive tax positions, and 150% for evasion. Criminal tax evasion under TAA 1994 section 143B can carry fines up to NZ$250,000 and/or imprisonment up to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% statutory NRWT on gross outbound dividends paid by a New Zealand company to a non-resident shareholder (Income Tax Act 2007 section RF 8). DTA relief commonly reduces portfolio dividends to 15% and direct substantial shareholding dividends to 5% or 10% depending on the applicable treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Double Tax Agreement rate, the non-resident recipient must: (1) obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority naming the beneficial owner; (2) complete Inland Revenue Form IR67, Non-Resident Withholding Tax Rate Reduction Application, declaring the relevant DTA article and beneficial ownership position; (3) provide the IR67 and TRC to the NZ payer before the dividend, interest, or royalty payment is made; (4) ensure the beneficial owner is not a conduit, pass-through, or fiscally transparent entity used to obtain treaty benefits; and (5) update the documentation annually or on any change in circumstances. Where NRWT was over-withheld at the statutory rate, the non-resident may claim a refund from the IRD using the appropriate refund/treaty application process within the statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT rates in New Zealand are 15% for outbound interest and 15% for outbound royalties. DTA provisions commonly reduce interest to 10% and royalties to between 0% and 10% depending on the intellectual property type and treaty partner. The Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) at 2% may apply to interest paid on registered public securities, but private intercompany loans generally remain subject to NRWT unless treaty relief is approved.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZ$5,000,000 aggregate cross-border related-party transactions in an income year triggers mandatory transfer pricing documentation preparation (Local File and Master File). Multinational groups with consolidated revenue exceeding EUR 750 million have separate CbC reporting obligations in New Zealand.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations. The IRD applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule in section BG1 of the Income Tax Act 2007, together with Part FV transfer pricing rules and DTA permanent establishment concepts, to require economic substance. The NZ_LTD entity must demonstrate that its Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) for data labeling, RLHF curation, annotation quality management, client contracting, payroll, and day-to-day decision making occur in New Zealand with real staff, premises, bank accounts, and governance records. A pure shell office passing invoices through a foreign parent is recharacterisable and subject to penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / deliberately false IR4 return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The director signs and files an IR4 that knowingly omits income from cross-border AI data-labeling and RLHF BPO services, fabricates subcontractor deductions, or shifts NZ-source revenue to an offshore related entity without a transfer pricing adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Administration Act 1994 section 141D imposes a shortfall penalty of 150% of the tax avoided. Section 143B makes tax evasion a criminal offence carrying fines up to NZ$250,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years for individuals; body corporates may be fined up to NZ$500,000 upon conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participate in or authorise the false return are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and shortfall penalties under TAA section 149A and Companies Act 1993 section 300. The court may pierce the corporate veil and order personal asset restitution, property seizures, IRD blacklisting, travel bans, company director disqualification, and imprisonment up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing manipulation / base erosion and profit shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging the offshore parent a highly inflated 40% service fee for non-existent management functions, while NZ_LTD reports persistent losses, fails to prepare Local File/Master File despite related-party transactions above NZ$5 million, and thereby erodes the New Zealand tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act 2007 Part FV (sections GC 13 to GC 24) allows the IRD to adjust income to the arm's length price, deny deductions for non-arm's length payments, and impose penalties under TAA section 141C (20%-40%) or section 141D (150%) for abusive tax positions. Failure to provide documentation when requested is a separate information-penalty offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve non-arm's length intercompany contracts are treated as parties to the avoidance arrangement. They may face civil liability for shortfall penalties, equitable compensation for breach of fiduciary duty under Companies Act section 131, personal liability for company debts in insolvency-based transactions, and criminal liability if false transfer pricing documents are created or certified.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using NZ_LTD as a no-substance shell that receives and passes AI training revenue through Mass_PayPal_Payout and Wise in artificially split tranches below NZD 10,000 to avoid AML/CFT monitoring thresholds, obscure beneficial owners, and conceal the true taxpayer from the IRD.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 sections 74-78 impose civil penalties up to NZ$300,000 for bodies corporate and NZ$60,000 for individuals for record-keeping, reporting, and due-diligence failures. Proceeds of Crime Act 2009 permits confiscation of assets derived from money laundering. Income Tax Act section BG1 voids the sham arrangement for tax purposes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts will pierce the corporate veil where the company is a mere façade. Directors face personal civil restitution, fines, director disqualification, travel bans, blacklisting, and criminal imprisonment. Knowingly structuring transactions to evade AML/CFT obligations can lead to imprisonment of up to two years; where the same conduct constitutes tax evasion, the imprisonment exposure increases to up to five years.
